title: Circular Measure Module 6 Lesson 1: Exact Values & Multiples of $\pi$ custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, values, configurations and requested combinations are original; mapped Cambridge evidence informs reasoning scope only.

parts.prompt: A circle has radius $12\text{ cm}$. Find the exact arc length of a sector subtending a central angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{6}\text{ radians}$ in terms of $\pi$.
A circle has radius $6\text{ cm}$. Find the exact area of a sector subtending a central angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{4}\text{ radians}$ in terms of $\pi$.

A circular sector of radius $6\text{ cm}$ has central angle $\dfrac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$. Find the exact area of the minor segment cut off by its chord in the form $a\pi - b\sqrt{3}$, where $a$ and $b$ are integers.
A circle of radius $8\text{ cm}$ has a chord that subtends a central angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$. Find the exact length of the chord.
A circle of radius $r$ is inscribed inside a square of side length $2r$. Express the exact area inside the square but outside the circle in terms of $r$ and $\pi$.
An annular sector has inner radius $2\text{ cm}$, outer radius $2\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$, and central angle $\dfrac{\pi}{6}\text{ radians}$. Find its exact area in terms of $\pi$.
A sector has radius $6$ cm and angle $\pi/3$. Find its arc length and area exactly.
